disclosure: rag-retrieval-v1.0 (R1-R5) saturated under BM25 because its questions share the wording of the guide titles and the template-generated corpus. After observing that limitation, v2.0 was designed as an audited symptom-to-case retrieval benchmark. The v2.0 specification was frozen before either BM25 or dense retrieval was run on it. R1-R5 remain in use for the answer-generation benchmark.

query_variants.note: the declared variant appends 'Component: <name>. Environment: <type>.' to the symptom

dense.query_prefix: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:

pre_registered.primary_comparison: bm25 / document / symptom_only  vs  dense / document / symptom_only
pre_registered.rule: Specification, queries, relevance judgments and configurations are frozen before the first run. No parameter, prefix, prompt or query is tuned afterwards, whichever retriever wins. Ablations are reported for discussion and never replace the primary configuration.

levels.strongly_relevant: same true root cause AND same component

root_cause_level.hit_at_k: 1 if any relevant document is in the top k
root_cause_level.capped_recall_at_k: |relevant in top k| / min(|relevant|, k): 1.0 means the top k are filled with relevant documents
root_cause_level.mrr: 1 / rank of the first relevant document (0 if none in the top 10)

case_similarity_level.strong_hit_at_k: 1 if any strongly relevant document is in the top k
case_similarity_level.strong_mrr: 1 / rank of the first strongly relevant document

abstention_retrieval_diagnostic.definition: AUROC of the top-1 retrieval score for separating answerable (positive) from no-answer queries
abstention_retrieval_diagnostic.note: retrievers always return documents; this only measures whether their top score carries a signal. Generator-level abstention accuracy is a separate, later benchmark

metrics.aggregation: macro average over the 40 answerable queries; the 5 no-answer queries are reported separately
metrics.uncertainty: queries sharing the same symptom text are perfectly correlated, so compare_runs.py reports a paired CLUSTER bootstrap (clusters = distinct symptom texts) with 95% intervals; the effective sample is the number of distinct texts, not 40

known_limitations.cause: symptom_summary is generated from 2-4 templates per root cause (frozen data layer), so several queries are textually identical
consequences: the effective sample size of the primary comparison is the number of distinct symptom texts, not 40
root-cause-level metrics are unaffected by duplicates (identical text implies identical root cause)

with symptom text only, strong (component-level) relevance cannot be fully resolved: the upper bounds above cap Strong-Hit@k for every retriever; the declared component+environment variant lifts that cap
this was found by the unit tests after the first freeze and BEFORE any retriever was run; the disclosure was added and the benchmark re-frozen once; no query and no relevance judgment changed
